memory_lessons.applicability: Independent per-element pricing has enough work to benefit from outer-loop parallelism on the largest supplied case; preserve thread-budget-aware dispatch and validate small cases for overhead.
memory_lessons.claim: The previous static-scheduled candidate was correct on all eight reported cases and measured 0.07160 seconds versus the 0.39098-second baseline. Since that candidate also extracted a per-element helper, the measured improvement cannot be attributed to parallel scheduling alone.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare whole-call timings for this explicit contiguous partition against the static-worksharing candidate over the same n/thread cases, including small serial-path cases.

proposal.hypothesis: The prior valid candidate used OpenMP static worksharing with a minimum of 256 elements per requested worker and measured 0.07160 seconds, but the loop scheduler's contribution is unknown. Retaining that dispatch policy while assigning contiguous ranges directly to each actual team member may reduce scheduling overhead for the uniform per-element pricing work. Using the actual team size also keeps all outputs covered if OpenMP forms a smaller team than requested. Candidate performance remains unmeasured.

retained: Extracted the per-element binomial calculation into a stack-local helper used by both serial and parallel paths; the arithmetic and terminal exponent sequence are unchanged.
Retained a serial path unless at least two requested workers can each receive at least 256 elements, bounding workers by both the supplied threads budget and available work.
Replaced OpenMP static loop scheduling with direct contiguous, balanced ranges based on the actual OpenMP team size; each output index is written once, and no global OpenMP controls are modified.
